ingestionProvenance.locator: printed p. 15 (PDF p. 18); printed p. 16 (PDF p. 19)

limitations.impact: supplier coverage rests partly on the non-respondent follow-up, the site visits and publicly available company information rather than on survey responses
limitations.statement: Printed p. 15: "a relatively low response rate — about 25 percent — to a survey sent to about 200 suppliers."

limitations.impact: the risk that respondents differ systematically from non-respondents was reduced by follow-up but never measured
limitations.statement: Printed p. 16: "the authors did not formally compare the respondents to the non-respondents — an additional analysis step that could have further mitigated concern about the response rate".

method: a written survey sent to about 200 suppliers of key parts of the various combat vehicles — engines, transmissions, radar and target acquisition components, and many other smaller parts (printed p. 15)

pointer.custodian: A.T. Kearney (the instrument and the responses, not public); U.S. Government Accountability Office (the published description)

respondents: about 25 percent responded; the authors contacted the non-respondents, and over 20 of them agreed to participate in the study site visits (printed pp. 15-16)

reviewers.name: U.S. Government Accountability Office
reviewers.role: method reviewed against research standards, consulting GAO specialists in survey and research methods

scopeOfValidity.builtToAnswer: Which suppliers of key combat vehicle parts can withstand enduring periods of low demand?

title: Written survey of about 200 suppliers of key combat vehicle parts, with non-respondent follow-up
